column13: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-08, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). TRAINING-DIAGNOSIS iter, NOT a hyperparameter tune. PRIOR: iter-1 (K=10) SSIM 0.285541 hr 0.0 PSNR 1.87 elapsed 321.5s; iter-2 (K=30) SSIM 0.285541 hr 0.0 PSNR 1.87 elapsed 946s -- BYTE-IDENTICAL to every digit, comparison.png identical (289606 B). iter-2 deepened the unroll 10->30 and the result did NOT change AT ALL -> depth is FALSIFIED as the limiter. SLURM TRAINING LOG (jobs 765204 iter-1 / 765283 iter-2) shows the smoking gun: loss=0.001739 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs, and the learnable step[k]=0.01, lambda[k]=0.001 PINNED at init for all 8 epochs -- the 20/60 scalars receive ZERO gradient and never move. FAILURE MODE (named): the supervised TV TRAINING is structurally frozen by a SATURATED-CLAMP gradient kill. Mechanism: data_grad = back_project(Rf - sino) is the RAW unfiltered adjoint of a 2304-view Mayo sinogram (sum-scaled, NO 1/N normalization). The classical tv_iterative sibling (SSIM 0.92) computes its gradient via AUTOGRAD on 0.5*mean(residual^2) -- a mean over 2304*736~1.7e6 elements -> per-element gradient ~1.7e6x SMALLER. tv_step_init=0.01 was inherited from the classical sibling's tv_lr but the supervised path's gradient is ~1.7e6x bigger, so f - 0.01*data_grad overshoots massively -> clamp(0,0.05) saturates the WHOLE image at K=1 -> the saturated clamp has derivative 0 everywhere -> no gradient reaches log_step/log_lambda -> scalars frozen, recon a near-constant clamped blob (PSNR 1.87, RMSE 0.0403) regardless of K. baseline LD-FBP PSNR=34.08 (Wagner-grade) confirms the data/projector are fine -- only the unrolled step scale is wrong. ONE CHANGE (un-stick training): tv_step_init 0.01 -> 1e-8 (operator-norm-matched: 0.01 / (2304*736) ~ 6e-9, rounded to 1e-8) so the unrolled iteration stays INSIDE the [0,0.05] clamp basin where the clamp is NOT saturated and gradients flow to the scalars. PAIRED ENABLER (not an independent knob -- with frozen gradients lr is inert): outer lr 5e-3 -> 5e-2 so the now-NONZERO scalar gradients move meaningfully across 8 epochs over the log-parametrised step/lambda. All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, val_n=214 ALL L277, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: with the step un-saturated, training un-freezes -- loss DECREASES across epochs, step[k]/lambda[k] DEPART from init, and SSIM rises from 0.2855 toward (and ideally above) the LD-FBP floor (~0.81) / the classical TV ceiling (SSIM 0.92, hr 0.205); even landing near the FBP baseline clears the 0.2855 collapse and proves the harness is repairable. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.286 (clamp still saturates) OR the scalars still don't move, the supervised-TV harness is STRUCTURALLY BROKEN on Mayo's 2304-view scale via the shared solver's unnormalized-adjoint step (which is FORBIDDEN to edit per the no-shared-module rule) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is not viable on real Mayo LDCT under the config-only contract) and STOP iterating this solver. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score): identical compute to iter-2 (K=30, same train/val sizes) -> ~946s, ~250s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted iter trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 either >0.81 (training un-froze, harness repaired) OR ~0.286 (structural -> negative result + STOP).

tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-05, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). RE-DIAGNOSIS from the iter-3 SLURM LOG (job 765340), which contradicts the iter-3 observation narrative: the 0.2855->0.8137 jump was NOT training un-freezing -- it is the LD-FBP PASSTHROUGH. Log facts: loss=0.000064 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs (did NOT decrease); lambda[k]=0.001 STILL PINNED at init for all 8 epochs (zero gradient); step[k] crept only 1.06e-8->1.76e-8. At tv_step_init=1e-8 the unrolled update f = f - step*(data_grad + lam*tv_grad) is scaled to ~zero, so the K=30 unroll is a near-identity map on fbp_init: pred ~= clamp(LD-FBP). That is why SSIM=0.8137 ~= the LD-FBP floor (~0.81), recon PSNR 33.60 is JUST BELOW baseline_PSNR 34.08, and hr=0.0 (the recon does not beat its own FBP). The freeze did not get fixed -- it MOVED: iter-1/2 (step=1e-2) froze via SATURATED-CLAMP (overshoot clamps the whole image, clamp derivative 0); iter-3 (step=1e-8) freezes via VANISHING-STEP (data+TV terms scaled to nothing, lam has no effect on the output so d loss/d lam ~= 0). FAILURE MODE (named): the limiter is the STEP SCALE, not depth (tv_K falsified iter-1->2) and not epochs/lr (lr=5e-2 already; scalars still don't move because the gradient to lambda is ~0 at both step extremes). The working step lives BETWEEN the two known-frozen regimes 1e-8 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-8 -> 1e-5 (the geometric midpoint sqrt(1e-8*1e-2)=1e-5 of the two frozen endpoints). At ~1e-5 the data-consistency term back_project(Rf-sino) actually moves the image OFF the FBP init across K=30 steps (so the recon depends on lambda -> non-zero gradient reaches log_lambda -> the 30 TV scalars can finally train), while staying INSIDE the [0,0.05] clamp basin (no whole-image saturation -> the clamp derivative is not 0 -> gradient also reaches log_step). Everything else IDENTICAL to iter-3 (lr=5e-2, K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-6, val_n=214 ALL L277, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0; tv_step_init STAYS finite/non-tiny -- do NOT revert toward 1e-8). HYPOTHESIS: with the step in the active basin, training un-freezes for REAL this time -- loss DECREASES across epochs, lambda[k] DEPARTS from 0.001 and step[k] adapts, and SSIM rises ABOVE the 0.8137 FBP passthrough toward the classical TV band (SSIM 0.85-0.92, the non-trained tv_iterative sibling hits 0.92 / hr 0.205); clearing hr>0 means the trained TV recon finally beats its own LD-FBP. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.81 with lambda STILL pinned (passthrough persists, the active basin is even narrower than 1e-5) OR collapses back toward ~0.286 (1e-5 already over-saturates the clamp), then the supervised-TV harness has NO step value that both trains the scalars AND beats FBP under Mayo's 2304-view unnormalized-adjoint scale within the config-only contract (the shared solver's raw back_project step is FORBIDDEN to edit) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is FBP-bounded on real Mayo LDCT) and STOP iterating this solver; iter-5 would only bracket the step further (e.g. 3e-6 / 3e-5) before declaring the negative. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score = 1200s wall): IDENTICAL compute to iter-3 (same K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, val_n=214, val_chunk=5 -- only the init VALUE of a scalar changes, not any loop size) -> ~918s measured iter-3, ~282s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 0.8137 (FBP passthrough, hr 0) -> iter-4 either >0.84 with lambda departing init and hr>0 (training un-froze for real) OR ~0.81 with lambda still pinned (passthrough -> bracket once at iter-5 then NEGATIVE RESULT + STOP).
